text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The United Nations Population Fund is proposing to provide Vietnam with $24 million for a population programme between now and the turn of the century.
-- A group of U.S. laywers and social activists have proposed a fund to support victims of Agent Orange.
-- Deputy Prime Minister Phan Van Khai said the government will guarantee sufficient supply of hard currency for industrial manufacturers importing materials and fuels for their production.
-- Ho Chi Minh City Party Chief Truong Tan Sang has called for religious organizations to take part in social programmes.
-- Vietnam exported 1.965 million tonnes of rice between January 1 and July 9.
-- Vietnam Airlines will start a new flight linking Ho Chi Minh City, Dalat and Danang on July 10.
-- Vietnam has set up a special department to control and supervise industrial technical safety in metallurgy, electronic production, mining and eletricity.
-- Deputy Prime Minister Phan Van Khai has ordered the authorities of Ho Chi Minh City to put more effort into the modernization of rural areas.
-- A new Voice of Vietnam radio transmitting station, which will cover the Mekong Delta area and Southeast Asian countries, has been put into operation.
